_strings.@@3fe28f1d2ffd: Oregon Surplus Credit ('kicker') — To be eligible for the 2025 kicker you must (1) file your 2024 Oregon return before you file your 2025 return, (2) have had an Oregon personal income tax liability for 2024, and (3) file a 2025 Oregon return even if you do not otherwise have a filing requirement. _strings.@@628054ce6bcd: Exemption Credit — Filers whose federal AGI is $100,000 or less (single or married filing separately) or $200,000 or less (all other statuses) may claim a credit for the exemptions claimed on line 6 of the return — regular exemptions for the taxpayer, spouse and dependents, plus severe-disability exemptions and exemptions for children with a qualifying disability. Above those AGI thresholds the credit is 0. The severe-disability and disabled-child counts drop out once federal AGI exceeds $100,000 for any status.
_strings.@@79d6967bf6cd: 2025 Form OR-40 Instructions (150-101-040-1, Rev. 01-29-26) — 'April 15, 2026 is the due date for filing your return and paying your tax due'; 'Your 2025 Oregon tax is due April 15, 2026' even on extension (Oregon accepts the federal extension; the extended filing due date is October 15, 2026, but an extension of time to file is not an extension of time to pay — pay the tax you expect to owe by April 15, 2026 or interest and penalties accrue).
_strings.@@85e5425a87e3: Oregon Kids Credit — You must (1) use a filing status other than married filing separately, (2) have one or more dependents age five or younger at the end of 2025 listed on your Oregon return, and (3) have qualifying income under $31,550 (income after subtractions with excluded foreign earned income and total losses over $20,000 added back, and with deducted tip income, overtime wages and passenger vehicle interest added back). A child listed as your dependent only because the custodial parent released the exemption to you does not qualify; a custodial parent may claim the credit even if the exemption was released.
_strings.@@895539c1fb45: Form OR-40-P (part-year resident) or Form OR-40-N (nonresident), 2025 — instructions 150-101-048-1; a part-year or nonresident filer prorates deductions, the federal tax liability subtraction and certain credits by the Oregon percentage.
_strings.@@8e6017f82175: Political Contribution Credit — Filers whose federal AGI is not more than $75,000 ($150,000 on a joint return) who made cash contributions during 2025 to a qualifying candidate, political party, or political action committee.
_strings.@@8e74b2f2b984: Treaty conformity — OR conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from OR income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the OR return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Oregon's resident return (Form OR-40) starts from federal adjusted gross income: 2025 Form OR-40 line 7 is the filer's federal AGI from Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 11 (or Form 1040-X, line 1C). Oregon taxable income is then built by applying additions (Schedule OR-ASC) and subtractions to that federal AGI. The 2025 OR-40 instruction booklet contains no general addition/add-back of federally treaty-exempt income (unlike California's Schedule CA, or CT/MD/MS). Because federally treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal AGI on the 1040 and there is no Oregon addition code restoring it, the treaty exclusion flows through and is NOT re-taxed by Oregon -> conforms. Caveat: confirm against the full Schedule OR-ASC / OR-ASC-NP addition code list (Publication OR-CODES) and Publication OR-17 for any niche addition that could touch a specific treaty article.

Second pass: the FULL four-bracket 2025 Chart S / Chart J (4.75%, 6.75%, 8.75%, 9.9%; breakpoints $4,400 / $11,100 / $125,000 for S and $8,800 / $22,200 / $250,000 for J, with printed constants $209 / $661 / $10,627 and $418 / $1,323 / $21,256) as printed in the 2025 Form OR-40-N and OR-40-P Instructions (150-101-048-1, Rev. 12-30-25), p.21 '2025 Tax rate charts': https://www.oregon.gov/dor/forms/FormsPubs/form-or-40-n_or-40-p-inst_101-048-1_2025.pdf — the resident booklet's $50,000-and-over constants chain exactly onto that schedule (S: $661 + 8.75% x $38,900 = $4,064.75 -> printed $4,065; J: $1,323 + 8.75% x $27,800 = $3,755.50 -> printed $3,756), so both passes agree on every rate, breakpoint and constant.

calls.work_head: OR state income tax (2025, graduated brackets): taxable_base $45,670.00 — which must be the state's own income base derived from federal AGI plus/minus the state's additions and subtractions (NOT raw federal AGI when modifications apply) — minus standard deduction [married_filing_jointly (qualifying surviving spouse uses the married-filing-jointly column)] = $5,670 = $40,000.00; graduated tax on $40,000 [married_filing_jointly (qualifying surviving spouse uses the married-filing-jointly column) schedule]: 0.0475 x $8,800.00 (the $0-$8,800 bracket) = $418.00; 0.0675 x $13,400.00 (the $8,800-$22,200 bracket) = $904.50; 0.0875 x $17,800.00 (the $22,200-$250,000 bracket) = $1,557.50; total $2,880.00 -> $2,880

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: 2025 Form OR-40, line 20 'Tax (see instructions)'. Instructions p.16: 'Tax tables. Use the tax tables to find your tax if your taxable income on line 19 is less than $50,000.' and 'Tax rate charts. If your taxable income on line 19 is $50,000 or more, calculate your tax using the formula in the tax rate chart for your filing status. Use Chart S if your filing status is single or married filing separately. Use Chart J if your filing status is married filing jointly, head of household, or qualifying surviving spouse.' This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Base guidance: supply 2025 Form OR-40, line 15 'Income after subtractions' (line 9 income after additions minus line 14 total subtractions). Line 15 already reflects Oregon additions (Schedule OR-ASC) and all subtractions, including the line 10 federal tax liability subtraction (2025 limit $8,500; $4,250 married filing separately; phased down by federal AGI per Table 4 — $0 at AGI of $145,000 or more for single/MFS, and at $290,000 or more for MFJ/head of household/qualifying surviving spouse) and the new 2025 subtractions that mirror the federal tip-income, overtime-wage and passenger vehicle loan interest deductions plus the first-time home buyer savings account (FTHBSA) subtraction. The op subtracts only the Table 5 standard deduction to reach line 19 (Oregon taxable income) and applies the rate schedule to reproduce line 20. Filers who itemize for Oregon (line 16 Schedule OR-A amount larger than the standard deduction) or who claim the age-65-or-older/blind additional standard deduction must compute lines 16-19 on the form instead — the op models only the basic per-status standard deduction. Adjudication note (two-pass): base is federal_agi — Form OR-40 line 7 is federal adjusted gross income, and the caller supplies the pre-deduction Oregon figure (line 15) so the op can reproduce line 19 by subtracting the standard deduction. Vector exemption counts are zero BY DESIGN: Oregon's personal/dependent exemptions are the $256-per-exemption CREDIT on line 25 for 2025 (up from $249 in 2024), income-limited, never a base reduction — exemptions ship as {}. Every 2025 boundary was re-indexed upward from 2024 ($4,300 -> $4,400 and $10,750 -> $11,100 on Chart S; $8,600 -> $8,800 and $21,500 -> $22,200 on Chart J), while the $125,000 / $250,000 top-bracket thresholds and all four rates (4.75/6.75/8.75/9.9%) are unchanged; verified across the resident booklet's $50,000+ chart segments and the OR-40-N/OR-40-P full charts. Tax-table mandate below $50,000: the 2025 OR-40 instructions (line 20, p.16) REQUIRE the tax tables when Oregon taxable income (line 19) is less than $50,000. The table is built from the rounded chart constants at $100-band midpoints, so bracket math may differ by a dollar or two within a band — booklet Example 1: a single filer with taxable income $19,525 uses the $19,500-to-$19,600 row and enters $1,400 on line 20, where exact marginal math on this schedule is $1,398.44 -> $1,398. The filed form must use the table; the rate-chart formula applies only at $50,000 or more. Rounded printed constants: Chart S's published constants are the exact cumulative bracket sums rounded DOWN ($209 is exact; $661 vs $661.25 exact; $10,627 vs $10,627.50 exact; the $50,000+ segment prints $4,065, which is both the exact cumulative sum and the value chained from $661), so at and above $125,000 pure marginal bracket math (what this op computes) can be up to $1 HIGHER than the printed chart formula. Chart J's constants are rounded UP ($418 is exact; $1,323 vs $1,322.50 exact; $21,256 = $1,323 + 8.75% x $227,800 = $21,255.50 rounded, vs $21,255.00 exact; the $50,000+ segment prints $3,756 vs $3,755.00 exact), so Chart J formula results run about $1 HIGHER than marginal math — booklet Example 2: married filing jointly with taxable income $75,500 computes $3,756 + 8.75% x $25,500 = $5,987 on the chart, where exact marginal math gives $5,986.25 -> $5,986. One schedule covers married filing jointly, head of household, AND qualifying surviving spouse (Chart J / tax-table Column J) — head of household brackets are identical to MFJ, and qualifying surviving spouse maps to married_filing_jointly with no divergence. Single and married filing separately share Chart S / Column S. Oregon registered domestic partners (RDPs) use the married statuses with an 'as if' federal return. Oregon's personal/dependent exemption is a tax CREDIT, not a base reduction, and is NOT shipped as an exemption: Form OR-40 line 25 'Exemption credit' = $256 per exemption for 2025 (taxpayer, spouse, dependents, plus severe-disability and disabled-child exemptions), subtracted from tax after the rate applies; it is $0 when federal AGI exceeds $200,000 ($100,000 if single or married filing separately), and the severe-disability/disabled-child counts drop out above $100,000 for every status. The calc op does not model this credit. THE 2025 KICKER IS A CREDIT, NOT A RATE OR BASE CHANGE: Oregon's surplus credit returns on the 2025 return (it is claimed in odd tax years — 44.28% on 2023 returns, none on 2024 returns). For 2025 the kicker is 9.863% of the filer's 2024 total Oregon personal income tax liability, claimed on Form OR-40 line 32 in the same way as a payment (or donated to the State School Fund). Eligibility requires filing the 2024 return before the 2025 return, having had a 2024 Oregon liability, and filing a 2025 return even with no filing requirement. It never touches this rate schedule or the base — do not adjust brackets or the standard deduction for it. Standard-deduction gates NOT modeled: married filing separately gets $0 if the other spouse claims itemized deductions (the shipped $2,835 assumes the spouse claims the standard deduction); a non-U.S. citizen without permanent resident status gets $0 (but may itemize); a person claimable as a dependent on another return is limited to the larger of earned income plus $450 or the $1,350 minimum, capped at the basic amount for their status. Compute those cases on the form. Age 65-or-older/blind additional standard deduction NOT modeled: each applicable checkbox adds $1,200 (single or head of household) or $1,000 (all other filers) to the Table 5 amount — the booklet's example has a married-filing-jointly couple with one spouse who turned 65 by 1/1/2026 entering $6,670 ($5,670 + $1,000). Enter it on the form; this op applies only the basic per-status amount. Federal tax liability subtraction is already inside the caller-supplied base (OR-40 line 10 flows into line 15): the 2025 limit is $8,500 ($4,250 married filing separately), phased down by federal AGI per Table 4 (single: $8,500 under $125,000, then $6,800 / $5,100 / $3,400 / $1,700 in $5,000 steps to $0 at $145,000 or more; MFS: $4,250 under $125,000 stepping to $0 at $145,000 or more; MFJ/head of household/qualifying surviving spouse: $8,500 under $250,000, then $6,800 / $5,100 / $3,400 / $1,700 in $10,000 steps to $0 at $290,000 or more). Alternative tax computations on line 20 NOT modeled: Schedule OR-FIA-40 (farm income averaging, box 20a), Worksheet FCG in Publication OR-FCG (farm asset capital gain rate, box 20b), and Schedule OR-PTE-FY (Oregon qualified business income reduced tax rate, box 20c — an irrevocable election that must be made on the original return) replace the table/chart math when elected. Bracket source: the resident OR-40 booklet (p.32) prints Chart S/Chart J only for taxable income of $50,000 or more (the tax tables govern below that). The full four-bracket 2025 Chart S/Chart J, including the $4,400 / $11,100 and $8,800 / $22,200 breakpoints shipped here, is printed in the 2025 Form OR-40-N/OR-40-P instructions (150-101-048-1, Rev. 12-30-25) p.21, whose own worked examples corroborate the constants ('Tax on the first $22,200 $1,323 (from the chart)' for a joint filer with $76,200 of taxable income; 'Tax on the first $11,100 $661' for a single filer with $41,100).
